mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is inverse: lower rates predict positive returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day returns is non-negative (>=0) or the rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A lower CPIAUCSL level (indicating lower inflation) reduces real interest rate uncertainty and supports equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is inverse: lower CPI predicts positive returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between CPIAUCSL level and 20-day returns is non-negative (>=0) or the rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0%, it signals a deteriorating labor market, increasing recession risk and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. The threshold is set at 5.0% to capture early recession signals.
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE > 5.0%, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1700 thousand units, it indicates weakening consumer demand and economic slowdown, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. The threshold is set at 1700 to capture significant demand contraction.
failure_condition: In instances where HOUST < 1700, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between low FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL (indicating stable, accommodative monetary policy) drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is active only when both conditions are met: FEDFUNDS < 2.5% and CPIAUCSL < 192.0.
failure_condition: The interaction term (FEDFUNDS * CPIAUCSL) is not significant in predicting returns, or the rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising PAYEMS (labor force growth) and falling UNRATE (labor market tightening) signals strong economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is active when PAYEMS increases by >0.5% and UNRATE decreases by >0.2% in the past month.
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS change * UNRATE change) is not significant in predicting returns, or the rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased discount rates and reduced liquidity. The regime is defined by FEDFUNDS increasing by >0.3% per month for 3 months.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.3% per month for 3 months
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS rises >0.3% per month for 3 months, the 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion (HOUST > 1800 and GDPC1 growth > 1.0% quarterly), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to overheating and impending policy tightening. The regime is defined by the joint condition of HOUST above 1800 and GDPC1 growth above 1.0% in the last quarter.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST > 1800 and GDPC1 growth > 1.0% (qtrly), the 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.
